es: Reconocer will, would y always + continuo para hablar de conductas típicas o molestas de alguien.

teaching.en: My grandfather will sit in the garden for hours and hum old songs.
teaching.es: Mi abuelo se sienta en el jardín durante horas y tararea canciones antiguas.
teaching.explanationEs: Will + verbo base presenta una conducta típica: así es él, lo hace siempre.
segments: My grandfather will sit in the garden
for hours and hum old songs.
teaching.audioText: My grandfather will sit in the garden for hours and hum old songs.

teaching.en: When we were kids, my brother would snore so loudly that we heard him downstairs.
teaching.es: Cuando éramos niños, mi hermano roncaba tan fuerte que lo oíamos desde abajo.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo base cuenta una conducta repetida del pasado; solo sirve con acciones, no con estados.
segments: When we were kids, my brother would snore
so loudly that we heard him downstairs.
teaching.audioText: When we were kids, my brother would snore so loudly that we heard him downstairs.

teaching.en: My aunt is always complaining about the weather!
teaching.es: ¡Mi tía siempre se está quejando del tiempo!
teaching.explanationEs: Always + presente continuo: la costumbre molesta a quien habla; hay una queja.
teaching.audioText: My aunt is always complaining about the weather!

teaching.en: Sara is stubborn: she will never ask for help.
teaching.es: Sara es terca: nunca pide ayuda.
teaching.explanationEs: Will never + verbo base describe un rasgo de carácter, no una decisión de hoy.
teaching.audioText: Sara is stubborn: she will never ask for help.

teaching.en: Nina has a funny habit: she will always talk to her plants.
teaching.es: Nina tiene una manía graciosa: siempre habla con sus plantas.
teaching.explanationEs: Will + always sin -ing describe un rasgo con cariño; la queja aparece con always + presente continuo.
segments: Nina has a funny habit: she
will always talk to her plants.
teaching.audioText: Nina has a funny habit: she will always talk to her plants.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase presenta lo que hace él como rasgo típico suyo?

choices.text: My neighbour is watering his plants at the moment.
My neighbour will water his plants at six every morning.
My neighbour watered his plants yesterday.

feedback.es: Will + verbo base presenta la conducta como típica de él; las otras dos frases hablan de un momento concreto, ahora o ayer.

hint.es: Busca will + verbo base, sin un momento concreto.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando era pequeña, mi prima se sentaba bajo la mesa en cada tormenta.»

feedback.es: Sit es una acción repetida en el pasado, así que would + verbo base cuenta la costumbre.

hint.es: Es una costumbre del pasado con una acción que se repite.

origin.text: When I was little, my cousin ___ sit under the table in every storm.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases contiene una queja por una costumbre?

choices.text: Leo always remembers my birthday.
Leo will remember my birthday.
Leo is always forgetting my birthday!

feedback.es: Always + presente continuo añade molestia: el hablante critica la repetición. Las otras dos frases son neutras.

hint.es: Busca always entre be y un verbo en -ing.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con lo que expresa.

pairs: My dad will fall asleep in front of the TV.
We would swim in the river every summer.
Tom is always leaving his shoes on the floor!
My sister plays tennis on Saturdays.

feedback.es: Cada forma tiene su matiz: will = rasgo típico, would = pasado, always + continuo = queja y presente simple = dato neutro.

pairs: My dad will fall asleep in front of the TV.
We would swim in the river every summer.
Tom is always leaving his shoes on the floor!
My sister plays tennis on Saturdays.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué siente quien habla.

choices.text: The speaker is tired of this happening so often.
The speaker says it happened only once.
The speaker is happy because she found them.

feedback.es: Always + presente continuo («is always losing») expresa fastidio por algo que se repite.

origin.audio: Our teacher is always losing her glasses.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi abuela siempre está perdiendo las llaves.»

answer.text: My grandmother is always losing her keys

feedback.es: La queja se construye con be + always + verbo en -ing: is always losing.

prompt.es: En el texto sobre Nico, ¿qué frase es una queja actual?

choices.text: He will argue about football for hours.
He is always borrowing my pens!
He would sing in the kitchen at six.

feedback.es: «Is always borrowing» muestra la molestia de ahora; will describe su carácter y would, una costumbre de cuando eran pequeños.

origin.text: My cousin Nico is a character. He will argue about football for hours. When we were small, he would sing in the kitchen at six. Now he is always borrowing my pens!

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hacía el padre cuando eran niños.

choices.text: He sings in the hall every day now.
He sang in the hall only once.
He used to make a lot of noise with his singing.

feedback.es: Would + verbo base, con «when we were kids», cuenta una costumbre del pasado: cantaba fuerte cada mañana.

origin.audio: When we were kids, Dad would sing loudly in the hall every morning.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi hermano pequeño nunca comparte sus cosas; es así.»

feedback.es: Will never + verbo base describe un rasgo de carácter de hoy: «es así».

origin.text: Even today, my little brother ___ never share his things; that is just how he is.

prompt.es: Leo está harto de su vecino. ¿Qué frase expresa su queja?

choices.text: My neighbour is always playing loud music at night!
My neighbour played loud music last night.
My neighbour will play loud music tonight.

feedback.es: La queja por algo repetido lleva always + presente continuo; las otras frases hablan de una noche concreta.

origin.text: Leo está harto: su vecino pone música alta por la noche, una y otra vez.

prompt.es: Hoy ya no ocurre: ¿qué frase habla de una costumbre del pasado?

choices.text: We will play cards every Sunday evening.
We would play cards every Sunday evening.
We play cards every Sunday evening.

feedback.es: Would + verbo base cuenta una costumbre que ya no existe; will la presenta como rasgo de hoy y el presente simple, como dato actual.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi hermana siempre está cambiando de opinión.»

feedback.es: Tras always en una queja, el verbo va en -ing: is always changing.

origin.text: My sister is always ___ her mind.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi abuelo se pasa horas hablando de trenes.»

answer.text: My grandfather will talk about trains for hours
accepted: My grandfather will talk about trains for hours
My grandfather will talk for hours about trains

feedback.es: Will + verbo base presenta la conducta como típica de él; for hours puede ir antes o después del complemento.
